correctness.rationale: The signed five-neighborhood identity is exact, all nonboundary deletions share its signature set, and exactly four boundary positions remain. The vector-support relabeling lemma reduces all alphabet sizes to an exhaustive finite table of 1+32+243+1024+3125 local five-tuples; explicit standard-library code gives full-support counts (1,8,90,192,120). Pairwise disjoint endpoint changes and an order-five de Bruijn word give sharpness for every \(n\ge q^5+12\). A separately implemented global histogram deletion program confirms the q=2..5 witnesses. The displayed saturation lower bound follows from at most n deletion positions, not extrapolation from tests.

value.rationale: The exact sharp capacity of a noisy one-deletion length-three oriented read-frequency channel is a natural observation invariant, not a small arbitrary sample. The \(\(q^5\)\)-leading polynomial and asymptotically length-optimal universal witnesses exhibit a structural interaction of local edit collisions, alphabet support and endpoints. This supplies a reusable exact channel bound and a meaningful family of test objects, without claiming exact first saturation length.
